title: Completion of the move sweep
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $E$ inject optional $\Gamma$-symbols into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits, and let $e:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an injection. For a finite Turing machine $M$ over $\Gamma$, a binary word $x$, a configuration $c$ on the input obtained by applying $e$ letterwise to $x$, and an action $a$ of $M$, one step of the binary simulator from the move-sweep configuration at counter zero equals the encoded configuration of the result of applying $a$ to $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $\Gamma$ is finite and has decidable equality
$E$ is an injection from optional symbols to blocks
$e$ is an injection from bits to $\Gamma$
$M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$c$ is a configuration on the letterwise $e$-image of $x$
replaced:
One transition of the binary block-code simulator applied to the move-sweep
configuration (source configuration $c$, source action $a$) at counter $0$ yields the
encoded configuration of the result of applying $a$ to $c$; in particular the
simulator halts exactly when the next state of $a$ is absent.
